Overview

  • NETL published three carbon capture studies in 2022–2023.
  • Cost of Capturing CO2 from Industrial Sources* (Industrial Report).
       • Quantifies the performance of CO2 compression and solvent-based capture systems
     and their greenfield and retrofit costs of CO2 capture when applied at nine
       representative industrial sources.
       • Representative plant sizes and CO2 available for capture from each industrial plant
      were chosen based on literature review, vendor input, and other NETL studies, where
       appropriate.
       • This study does not characterize reference industrial plants beyond the flowrate and
      stream characteristics of the available CO2 stream. The production costs of each
       plant’s product before and after retrofit are not considered.
  • Cost and Performance of Retrofitting NGCC Units for Carbon Capture.**
       • Quantifies the cost and performance of retrofitting natural gas combined cycle
     (NGCC) power plants with solvent-based post-combustion carbon capture.

*Cost of Capturing CO2 from Industrial Sources is publicly accessible via https://www.osti.gov/biblio/1887586
**Cost and Performance Baseline of Retrofitting NGCC Units for Carbon Capture is publicly accessible via https://www.osti.gov/biblio/1961845

                                                                                         4

Overview (continued)

  •  Eliminating the Derate of Carbon Capture Retrofits.*

       • Quantifies options for existing pulverized coal (PC) boilers to reduce the effects caused
      by steam and power requirements of retrofit solvent-based capture systems and the
        resulting derated output of the existing plant.
       • Allows for addition of supplemental heat and power provisions in support of CO2
      capture (e.g., natural gas (NG)-fired boiler for solvent-regeneration heating needs and
    NG simple-cycle for combined heat and power supply).

  •  To accompany those studies, Microsoft Excel-based tools were developed to
    provide public users with the ability to perform high-level analysis on the
    incremental costs for retrofitting industrial plants and electricity generation units
    with CO2 capture and/or compression systems.





*Eliminating the Derate of Carbon Capture Retrofits is publicly accessible via https://www.osti.gov/biblio/1510790

   Databases (CCRDs).*
        • Publicly available spreadsheet tools

Overview
Limitations

• The cost and performance results presented in the CCRDs are based on
  assumptions necessitated by limitations of available data. These
  uncertainties compound those of the reference cost and performance
  data used as the basis for developing the reported results.

• The CCRDs are not meant to provide actual CO2 capture costs for any
  plant or sector—too many site-specific variables make such accuracy
  infeasible—but serve as a valuable tool for comparative analysis between
  plants within an industry or for comparing one industry to another (e.g.,
  comparing capture costs in the ammonia sector versus the cement sector).

Design Assumptions

•  In 2021, Shell provided quotes for two amine-based capture systems.

     • CANSOLV® post-combustion capture: quote for Cement and Iron/Steel (industrial)
      applications, quote for PC applications, and quote for NGCC applications.
     • ADIP-Ultra® pre-combustion capture: quote for Refinery Hydrogen (industrial) application.
  Each system was quoted at 90, 95, and 99% capture rates, except for NGCC,
  which was quoted at 90, 95, and 97% capture.
•  Other vendor quotes for an NG boiler, NG simple-cycle combustion turbine, and
  reciprocating CO2 compressor were obtained from various original equipment
  manufacturers in support of recent NETL studies, including those used to develop
  the CCRDs.
•  Retrofit costs were estimated for all cases by applying a factor to the total plant
  cost (TPC) of incremental capital equipment required to support CO2 capture.
     • This includes, but is not limited to, items such as the solvent-based capture system; other gas
     clean-up unit operations; CO2 compression, cooling, and drying equipment; and ancillary
     equipment and facilities.


                                                                                       8

Design Assumptions (continued)

  • Aspen Plus® simulations of each representative capture system were created to
    provide process parameters used to scale capital costs and estimate annual
    operating and maintenance (O&M) costs for consumables, waste disposal, fuel,
   power, and co-product costs, as applicable.
        • For industrial cases, only the CO2 capture systems—and the NG boiler used to raise steam
         for solvent regeneration, where necessary—were modeled based on assumptions made to
       characterize the emissions streams leaving each representative industrial plant.
               •  Industrial capture system auxiliary load demands are met with power purchased from the grid.
        • For NGCC and PC cases, the entire power generation plant is modeled to account for
       derate due to the additional auxiliary load demands of the capture system and steam
       extraction required for solvent regeneration heating needs.
  •  Capital costs were scaled per guidance in the latest revision of NETL’s QGESS
    Capital Cost Scaling Methodology: Revision 4 Report.*

  •  Per NETL’s QGESS Cost Estimation Methodology for NETL Assessments of Power
    Plant Performance,* some O&M costs are calculated based on TPC (e.g.,
   maintenance labor, property taxes and insurance, and maintenance materials).

*NETL maintains a library of Quality Guidelines for Energy System Studies (QGESS) that is used to guide technoeconomic analyses. The QGESS documents are referenced within the report; the CCRD tool and are publicly accessible via
https://netl.doe.gov/node/7513

Financial Methodology
Calculating the COC for Industrial Cases
• The COC for industrial cases, excluding transport and storage (T&S), is
  calculated using the equation below, where T&S costs would be an
  additive cost if included.


                                $     𝑇𝑂𝐶∗𝐶𝐶𝐹+ 𝐹𝑂𝑀+ 𝑉𝑂𝑀+ 𝑃𝐹+ 𝑃𝑃
                          =
                         𝑡𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝐶𝑂2      𝑡𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑠𝐶𝑂2 𝑐𝑎𝑝𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒𝑑𝑝𝑒𝑟𝑦𝑒𝑎𝑟

• Where:
     • TOC – Total overnight costs of all equipment added to support capture application.
     • CCF – Capital charge factor based on industry-specific financial assumptions.
     • FOM – Annual fixed O&M costs.
     • VOM – Annual variable O&M costs.
     • PF – Purchased NG fuel.
     • PP – Purchased power.


                                                                                       11

Financial Methodology
  Calculating the COC for Power Cases
  •  The COC for power cases, excluding T&S, is calculated using the equation below, where
    T&S costs would be an additive cost if included.

                               $      𝐶𝑂𝐸+ 𝑀𝑃𝐶−𝑇𝑆−𝐼𝐹𝑂𝑀∗𝑃𝑅𝐶−𝑇𝑃𝐿
                          =
                         𝑡𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝐶𝑂2        𝑡𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑠𝐶𝑂2 𝑐𝑎𝑝𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒𝑑𝑝𝑒𝑟ℎ𝑜𝑢𝑟
  •  Where:
        • COE – Cost of electricity including T&S, $/megawatt-hour (MWh).
        • MPC – Makeup/excess power cost, $/MWh.
                • Accounts for the cost of derate to the existing plant gross output, or in cases where NG simple cycle
           power and heat generation are added, a credit when power is produced over the existing plant gross
            output less total auxiliary load demand.
        • TS – CO2 T&S costs, $/MWh.
                • T&S costs are estimated based on guidance in NETL’s QGESS Carbon Dioxide Transport and Storage
             Costs in NETL Studies* for default cases but is a manipulatable user input in the CCRDs.
        • IFOM – Incremental change in existing plant fixed O&M, $/MWh.
        • PRC – Pre-retrofit capacity, megawatt (MW).
        • TPL – Parasitic retrofit load, MW.
*NETL maintains a library of QGESS that is used to guide technoeconomic analyses. The QGESS documents are referenced within the report; the CCRD tool and are publicly accessible via https://netl.doe.gov/node/7513
